toc.title: Requirement Words and What They Point To

html:
1What You Will Learn

Note

Acronyms in this note. EMR: Elastic MapReduce; MSK: Managed Streaming for Apache Kafka; BI: business intelligence; MWAA: Managed Workflows for Apache Airflow; PII: personally identifiable information; SCP: service control policy; EC2: Elastic Compute Cloud; DMS: Database Migration Service; ML: machine learning; IAM: Identity and Access Management

  • A pacing plan for 65 questions in 130 minutes
  • A four-step method for every question
  • How distractors are built on this exam, and how to see through them
  • A final-week plan and exam-day checklist

2Pacing

Running case

Kestrel Freight's Data Engineer Sits the Exam

  • 65 questions in 130 minutes, with a data pipeline in nearly every scenario
  • Some questions are long, and every option looks reasonable
  • The engineer wants a pace, a method and a way to read distractors
  • Your job: build that routine before exam day

  • 65 questions in 130 minutes is 2 minutes each; aim for about 100 seconds on a first pass so there is time for long scenarios and review
  • Checkpoints (latest): question 20 by minute 40, question 40 by minute 80, question 65 by minute 120, then 10 minutes to review flagged questions
  • 15 questions are unscored and not marked: give every question full attention
  • Never leave a question blank: a guess costs nothing and a blank scores zero
  • Flag and move on when stuck (after about 2 minutes); come back if time remains
Exam tip

Use any spare time to re-read the requirement word of the flagged questions; most misses come from a missed word, not a missed service.

3A Four-Step Method

  1. Read the last line first. It says what to choose and what counts ("most cost-effective", "least operational overhead", "near real time", "most secure")
  2. Predict the service or setting before you read the options
  3. Eliminate options that are clearly wrong (wrong data model, wrong latency, too much operations, a long-term key)
  4. Confirm the remaining option meets every requirement in the scenario, including the verb (ingest, transform, orchestrate, secure, audit)
Exam tip

On multiple response, find each correct option on its own merits; if the question says "Select TWO", the answer has exactly two.

4Requirement Words and What They Point To

Words in the question Usually points to
Least operational overhead, serverless, fully managed Glue, Athena, Firehose, Step Functions, Lambda, EMR Serverless, Redshift Serverless, DynamoDB on-demand
Near real time, seconds, replay, multiple consumers Kinesis Data Streams (or MSK); enhanced fan-out
Load into S3/Redshift with no code Amazon Data Firehose
Lowest cost for occasional SQL on S3 Athena + Parquet + partitions
Heavy, concurrent BI queries on structured data Redshift
Key lookup, single-digit millisecond, unpredictable traffic DynamoDB (on-demand)
Existing Airflow / Kafka / Cassandra / MongoDB MWAA / MSK / Keyspaces / DocumentDB
Exactly once, long running, auditable workflow Step Functions Standard
Wait for a job to finish Step Functions .sync
Reprocess, backfill, rewind Retention + replay, Glue bookmark reset, raw data in S3
Row-level updates and time travel in a lake Apache Iceberg / S3 Tables
Centralized permissions on lake data Lake Formation
Rotate credentials automatically Secrets Manager
Who did it / what changed CloudTrail / Config
Find PII Macie
Keep data in a Region SCP with aws:RequestedRegion

5How the Distractors Work

  • Real service, wrong job: for example Firehose where replay is required, EMR where least overhead is required, DynamoDB for ad hoc SQL joins, Redshift for a single-key lookup
  • Too much work: a custom Lambda or EC2 solution when a managed feature exists (AppFlow, DMS, Glue bookmarks, Lake Formation, Secrets Manager rotation)
  • Insecure shortcut: long-term access keys, 0.0.0.0/0, "Action": "*", passwords in code
  • Right idea, wrong scope: a bucket policy where column-level control is needed; CloudWatch where who is needed
  • Half the requirement: meets speed but not cost, or durability but not ordering
  • A feature that does not exist or is out of scope: ML training, language syntax, services on the out-of-scope list
Exam tip

When two options both work, choose the one that is more managed, more secure by default, or named by the requirement word (cost, speed, overhead).

6Final Week and Exam Day

  • Days 7 to 5: re-read the Quick Reference Cards of Domain 1 (34%) and Domain 2 (26%); redo the questions you got wrong
  • Days 4 to 3: Domains 3 and 4; the look-alike table in Module 19
  • Day 2: the requirement-word table (section 4) and the numbers table; one timed block of 20 questions
  • Day 1: light review and sleep; no new topics
  • Exam day: arrive or log in early; photo ID and a clear desk for online proctoring; read each question fully; watch the clock against the checkpoints
  • Booking and rules change [Verify live]: the exam fee, languages and retake rules are on the AWS certification page; the exam is valid for three years and renewed by taking the current exam
  • After the exam: the result is pass or fail with a scaled score; a report by section shows strengths and gaps

7Exam Q&A

7.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer; some ask for two)

S1A question asks for the solution with the LEAST operational overhead to deliver streaming data to Amazon S3 as Parquet. Two options both work: one uses Amazon Data Firehose and one uses a custom consumer on EC2. Which should be chosen?

  • AThe custom consumer on EC2
  • BNeither
  • CEither, because they are equal
  • DAmazon Data Firehose
Show the answer

Answer: D. Least operational overhead points to the managed, serverless service.

S2A candidate has used 85 minutes and has answered 38 of 65 questions. What should they do?

  • ASpend five minutes on each remaining question until the time runs out completely
  • BLeave the last ten questions blank because blanks cost nothing
  • CStop and restart the exam so that the timer starts again
  • DSpeed up to about 100 seconds per question, flag hard ones and keep moving
Show the answer

Answer: D. At question 38 by minute 85 the candidate is behind the checkpoint of question 40 by minute 80, so they should pick up the pace, flag difficult questions and answer every question.

S3A question tells the candidate to choose two answers and lists five options. What is the best approach?

  • APick the first two options that sound plausible and move on to the next question quickly
  • BPick three options to be safe, because extra picks cost nothing
  • CPick none of the options and flag the question for later
  • DJudge each option against the requirement and choose exactly two correct ones
Show the answer

Answer: D. Multiple response questions have the stated number of correct options, and each must be judged on its own.

S4Which clue in a question most directly suggests Amazon Kinesis Data Streams over Amazon Data Firehose?

  • AThe data must be loaded into S3 with no code at all and no custom consumers
  • BThe team wants no capacity management of any kind
  • CThe data must be replayed by several independent consumers
  • DThe data arrives as a single nightly file from a warehouse
Show the answer

Answer: C. Replay and multiple custom consumers need a durable stream; Firehose delivers without replay, and a nightly file is a batch case.

S5An answer option uses long-term access keys stored in a script to let a pipeline read S3. How should the candidate treat it?

  • ATreat it as the best answer, because keys in a script are simple to use
  • BTreat it as a likely distractor, because an IAM role with temporary credentials is the secure choice
  • CTreat it as correct if the keys are rotated once a year by hand
  • DTreat it as equal to a role, because both give access to S3
Show the answer

Answer: B. Long-term keys in scripts are an insecure shortcut; roles provide temporary credentials and are the expected answer.

8Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Pacing 65 questions, 130 minutes, ~100 seconds first pass; Q20 by minute 40, Q40 by 80, Q65 by 120; flag after ~2 minutes; never leave blank
Method Read the last line first → predict → eliminate → confirm requirement word and verb
Multiple response Exactly the number asked; judge each option alone
Requirement words Least overhead → managed/serverless; near real time/replay → Kinesis; no-code load → Firehose; centralized lake permissions → Lake Formation
Distractors Real service, wrong job; too much work; insecure shortcut; wrong scope; half the requirement
Final week Domains by weight, redo misses, look-alike table, timed block, sleep; check AWS certification page for rules
